We are directing this machine toward the grand challenges of biology and materials science. Our mission is to build the machine that discovers the next Transformer, the next AlphaFold, and the breakthroughs that push science and engineering to the absolute frontier.

Ashr is a fully contained test and evals platform that improves AI agents by ensuring accuracy and quality across a wide range of user journeys through your product.

Ashr generates user journeys through your agents’ tool calls, results, and questions. We don’t generate one off tests, we generate large amounts of authentic user stories through your product, and pick up on errors, inconsistencies, and failures that would otherwise take hours of manual testing or get caught by a customer. We also work to ensure agent response quality in line with your business goals by offering custom evaluation metrics.

Ashr works with voice, text, automated website generation, image, file generation, and multimodal. We’re also willing to generate custom input types or make modifications for anyone interested. Currently, we integrate as an SDK, and are proactively working to make our documentation and resources as accessible and easy to use as possible.
long_description.after:
Ashr Manifold is a self-contained model training, hosting, observability, and continual learning platform for purpose-built open-weight models. 

Startups can use Manifold to post-train and manage fleets of continuously improving open-weight models without having a dedicated research team or infrastructure. Ultimately, this reduces operating costs and allows a greater degree of control over proprietary company knowledge.

Enterprises can use Manifold to encode institutional judgements and priorities into open-weight models, reduce token costs, and manage every level of the AI life cycle, from data curation, to model serving on weights and infrastructure they own.

one_liner.after: Enterprise post-training, monitoring, and continual learning platform

long_description.before:
In investment management, the final outcome isn't a deck or a memo. It's the trade. 

Kimpton is the AI-native research platform for portfolio managers. We're commoditizing the research layer and handing PMs data distilled into structured trades. 

The whole industry is fighting underperformance. Active managers trail their benchmarks, and capital keeps bleeding into passive. AI was supposed to fix that, but it hasn't. Funds either stitch together a dozen point tools or babysit general agents all day, and neither gets them to the trade. 

Kimpton goes straight to it. It ingests a fund's mandate, strategy, and positions. It runs them through our own harness and returns a structured trade proposal built for that fund. It connects to any institutional data source they already run on. And it's built to disagree, because consensus is poison for investment decisions. Instead of telling a PM what they want to hear, it surfaces the breaches and risks they'd otherwise miss. 

We're two ex-Goldman engineers and an ex-SpaceX engineer. We left to start our own quantitative systematic hedge fund. We raised $10M from a family office at 21 and 22, and scaled it to $35M over four years. We built Kimpton inside that fund, then productized the stack. 

We're live with our first institutional client, a $3.3B manager, and our first market is fundamental equity funds from $1B to $10B.

Humans make the decisions. Kimpton does everything else.
long_description.after:
In investment management, every decision gets graded. The market prints the answer on a date known in advance, and nobody gets to argue with it.

Kimpton is financial AI that answers to reality. Kimpton OS is the AI-native operating system for investment teams: it does the research and hands PMs structured trades. EarningsBench is a public benchmark where models forecast quarterly earnings before companies report and the reported numbers do the scoring. Koliseum is the set of point-in-time financial environments we build from that work, for labs to train and evaluate models on.

The whole industry is fighting underperformance. Active managers trail their benchmarks, and capital keeps bleeding into passive. AI was supposed to fix that, but it hasn't. Funds either stitch together a dozen point tools or babysit general agents all day, and neither gets them to the trade.

Kimpton OS goes straight to it. It ingests a fund's mandate, strategy, and positions, connects to the institutional data the fund already runs on, and returns a structured trade proposal built for that fund. It's built to disagree, because consensus is poison for investment decisions. Instead of telling a PM what they want to hear, it surfaces the breaches and risks they'd otherwise miss.

That same work is how we grade AI. Static benchmarks leak into training data. Simulations reward what their authors imagined. A forecast sealed before the outcome exists and scored when the company reports can't be rehearsed or backdated. We started in markets because they're the one place reality answers on schedule.

We're two ex-Goldman engineers and an ex-SpaceX engineer. We left to start our own quantitative systematic hedge fund, raised $10M from a family office at 21 and 22, and scaled it to $35M over four years. We learned to trust live results over historical fit. We built Kimpton inside that fund, then productized the stack.

We're live with our first institutional client, a $3.3B manager. Our first market is fundamental equity funds from $1B to $10B, and the labs that need to know whether their models can do this work.

one_liner.after: Live Evaluation Arenas for Financial Work

Armature helps companies monitor, analyze, and optimize how AI agents experience their products.

We start with Product Analytics: user sessions on your Claude Connector, ChatGPT App or MCP live inside their AI client, not your UI. Armature captures and shows you what users ask, what agents think and how they use your product.

Then, we provide automated evals infrastructure: run complex sessions against your MCPs/CLIs across all major harnesses and models to catch broken workflows before your users do.

Finally, our MCP lets your internal coding agents plug into Armature to autonomously fix your product's AX based on our run data.

The next step is to provide the foundational infrastructure for the Agent Experience, powering agent-native revenue, lifecycle marketing, and customer support for the next generation of software.

Once agents use your product, Armature shows you what users do with it through AI, with self-serve MCP analytics and evals that catch regressions before your users see them.

long_description.before:
Our first model, Atom 1, pre-trained on the internets video, and fine tuned for physics, already tops the Physics IQ benchmark.
It has been action conditioned, so you can simulate robot actions within it.
This lets Robot Labs check every checkpoint, getting you results in minutes; instead of having to wait days for human evaluations. 
It also lets you simulate unseen and hard to replicate environments.

A world model good enough to grade robots is a world model good enough to drive one!
Our second core bet is to design our robot model (world action model) to be micromanaged by LLMs, allow robotics to use the orchestration and planning abilities of LLMs while having the physics, contact and timing be controlled by the robot model (world action model).

long_description.before:
Osseus is the intelligent development platform for robotics. It plugs into the tools a team already uses - CAD, ECAD, GitHub, Jira, docs, messaging, and test runs - creating a live dependency graph of their entire robot stack. It automatically builds and maintains the relationships between every part, board, requirement, test, and decision.

When a hardware change is made, the map traces the downstream impact across mechanical, electrical, and software. Osseus's agents find which requirements may be compromised, run the attached tests and sims, create fixes for the affected hardware/software on branches, and re-run the tests to confirm the new design doesn’t break downstream.

Osseus includes a robotics component marketplace. Teams can list spare parts and hardware for others to buy/rent during prototyping, and designs can be evaluated against real component availability. If a part has a long lead time or is unavailable, engineers can quickly find compatible alternatives in their area instead of waiting weeks or asking around their network.

Design review also happens in Osseus. Engineers see why a design might not work, what's been tried before, and why something was built the way it was, pulled from prior conversations between engineers and with suppliers. Suppliers comment directly on a part through a secure link instead of back and forth over email, and what they say is remembered. If a supplier flags that a design isn't machinable, or that changing a feature would cut cost, that insight automatically appears the next time someone designs something similar, saving time and money.

We ultimately will use the platform's deep engineering understanding to develop physical-AI models that reason jointly over the robot's geometry, electronics, kinematics, components, software, and real-world performance so people can optimize and iterate on robots much faster. Get in touch to learn more!
Predictive maintenance for the power grid.
long_description.after: At Talos, we are building better, more modern predictive maintenance for the power industry with a focus on large transformers. Our devices continuously monitor critical power equipment and detect problems early on using anomaly-detection models. For each fault, we provide detailed analyses of the problem, exactly where and why it happened, as well as next steps teams should take.
